statement: From every subsequence of sizes tending to infinity there is a further subsequence and a representation coupling on which the following properties hold almost surely, simultaneously. The limiting sphere in these coordinates has the ordinary unit-area √ 3-LQG law, with area µh and metric Dh; the latter induces the round topology. (i) Geometry in one coordinate. (2.5) The maximum round diameter of the embedded flags tends to zero. Consequently the maximum round diameter of an embedded primal edge tends to zero as well. (ii) One Hilbert space. There is an order vn(i), 0 ≤ i < 2n, of the primal corner occurrences and a continuous tour η : [0, 1] → S2 such that η∗ dt = µh, sup 0≤t<1 ρ (︁ zn(vn(⌊2nt⌋)), η(t) )︁ −→ 0. (2.6) Each vertex v occurs deg(v) times in the corner list. For µh-almost every z, the fiber η−1({z}) contains exactly one time. With H = L2([0, 1], dt), the maps Jn : L2 (µn) −→ H, (Jnu)(t) = u(vn(⌊2nt⌋)), 0 ≤ t < 1, J : L2 (µh) −→ H, Jf = f ◦ η are isometries, and J is unitary. In particular, ∥Jn(f ◦ zn) − Jf∥L∞([0,1]) −→ 0 (f ∈ C(S2 )). (2.7) (iii) Centered inverse convergence. The closed continuum form Eh is a regular Dirichlet form and is the form of Liouville Brownian motion with the stated half-energy clock. Its operator G has kernel exactly the constants. For a nonnegative operator whose kernel is the constants, write A† for its inverse on the mean-zero subspace, extended by zero on constants. Let Π be the orthogonal projection onto the constants in H, and put Kn = Jn(2Gn)† J∗ n, K = J(2G)† J∗ . (2.8) Thus Kn is also zero on Jn(L2(µn))⊥. These are bounded positive self-adjoint operators, and ∥Kn − K∥HS −→ 0. (2.9) 5 (iv) Local recovery with unit conductivity. There are ordinary conformal chart domains whose interiors cover S2. Let V ⋐ W ⋐ U be open sets with U compactly contained in one of these charts, and let χ be a real smooth function on S2 satisfying 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and supp χ ⊂ V . There are local vertex functions ˜︁ wn, defined on graphs containing all incidences needed over W, that converge uniformly to χ on a neighborhood of W, in the vertex locations, and satisfy lim sup n ∑︂ e: zn(e)∈W (de ˜︁ wn)2 ≤ ∫︂ U |∇χ|2 dvol. (2.10) Here zn(e) is any chosen point on the embedded edge, and the integral is the unhalved conformal Dirichlet integral. Every edge is counted with its multiplicity. If one endpoint lies in a fixed compact subset of W, then eventually its entire edge, both endpoints, and all the required incidences lie in W, uniformly over such edges. The assertions in (iv) hold simultaneously for these buffered tests on the coupled outcome, so the tests may be chosen after fixing that outcome.
